name: Karbonsteel Engineering Ltd
title: Karbonsteel Engineering Ltd - 544511 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Heavy fabricator guides to 40,000 tons and 12-13% normalised margin on a 54,000-ton expansion, but the expansion slipped from March to October and FY25 revenue missed the 340-crore target.

capex.quote: This expansion is underway, with a revised completion timeline of October 2025.

triggers.label: Revenue target 340 cr missed
triggers.quote: Some labor jobs were the reason we did not reach our ideal revenue levels of 340 crores.

triggers.label: Inventory days 160 → 130
triggers.quote: We improved from 160 days last year to 130 days in FY25.

triggers.label: Steel pass-through via PV clauses
triggers.quote: we passed on steel price increases through price variation (PV) clauses.

They should be around 4-5% for FY26 and move above 5% for FY27.

summary.headline: Karbonsteel crossed ₹300 crore revenue in FY26 with 10.86% EBITDA margin and ₹10.51 crore PAT, which management says normalises to ₹16.56 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue crossed ₹300 crore, but the company missed its ₹340 crore ideal level because of Khopoli exit, labour migration after the March LPG force majeure, and a ~₹40 crore shortfall from low-value labour jobs. Reported EBITDA margin was 10.86% and PAT ₹10.51 crore, including a ₹1.65 crore NCLT bad-debt write-off, ₹2.4 crore rent for the delayed Umargam expansion and Khopoli shifting costs. Order book was stated at about ₹350 crore as of May, up from near ₹200 crore. The Umargam expansion from 30,000 to 54,000 tonnes slipped from March to October 2026.

segments.name: Heavy and precision structural fabrication
segments.commentary: Core business; 70-80% of FY26 tonnage was complex custom work. Realisation about ₹100/kg for full fabrication versus ~₹30/kg for labour-only jobs; conversion margin ₹30-45/kg.

segments.name: PEB
segments.commentary: Revenue contribution fell to 0%; management says it will remain a small part as the company focuses on production rather than erection.

segments.name: Railways / bullet train
segments.commentary: Bullet train work (4,500 tonnes) was largely booked in the prior year; FY26 contribution nominal. Railway product development is at a very early stage.

guidance_outlook: Normalised EBITDA margin of 12-13% expected going forward; H2 FY26 normalised EBITDA cited at ~14%.
Production target ~40,000 tonnes annually at ~₹100/kg; FY26 utilisation guided at 80-90%.
PAT margin ~4-5% for FY26 and above 5% for FY27; aspiration of 7-8% later.
Finance costs guided at ~4% of turnover in FY26; FY27 targeted revenue ₹400 crore with order book of at least ₹500 crore.
Automation expected to add 15-20% efficiency; automation alone contributes ~1% EBITDA margin uplift by FY28.
Long-term aspiration of ₹800-1,000 crore revenue and 7,000-8,000 tonnes per month, requiring post-FY27 expansion funded by internal accruals and equity.
Labour expected to return by end-June 2026; ~₹150 crore order pipeline expected around September-October.
capex_capacity: Umargam expansion from 30,000 to 54,000 tonnes; completion revised to October (management cited 'October 2025' in places, which appears to be a transcription error given the call date of June 2026); initially targeted March.
₹21 crore work-in-progress on the expansion; another ₹10-15 crore capex planned next year, split between shed/building and automation.
Sheds 1 and 2 about 60% complete; a blasting machine under installation; automation planned in cutting, automatic beam welding and fit-up centre.
1 MW solar plant in two phases at ~₹3-3.5 crore, expected online October-November; expected to cut power bills by over 50%. Energy cost ~₹25-30 lakh per month.
Khopoli facility (2.5 acres, rented) exited, removing ~5,000-6,000 tonnes of capacity; team consolidated at Umargam (20+ acres).
demand_pricing: Order book grew from ~₹200 crore to ~₹350 crore as of May; management targets at least ₹500 crore of orders against a ₹400 crore revenue target.
90-95% of orders are repeat business; clients include ArcelorMittal, a major Maharashtra steel company, two large business houses and a power company.
MOU signed for 15,000 tonnes specifically for data centres.
Steel prices rose from ₹50-55/kg to ₹65-70/kg; price variation clauses pass through most steel cost, but conversion and transport fixed portions are being accepted gradually.
Management says PEB peers realise ₹115-120/kg but are EPC contractors; not comparable as Karbonsteel only manufactures.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EBITDA margin rise only 1% by FY28 if one-offs disappear?
qa_highlights.answer: The 1% uplift is attributed to automation alone; other improvements are expected beyond that. Normalised margin expected at 12-13%.

qa_highlights.question: Expected production and utilisation after expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40,000 tonnes annually at ~₹100/kg; FY26 utilisation 80-90%. Full 54,000-tonne capacity targeted for the following year.

qa_highlights.question: Solar capex and savings?
qa_highlights.answer: ₹3-3.5 crore for the solar plant, cutting bills by over 50%; eventually 100% solar power. Automation like laser cutting deferred until solar is in place due to power intensity.

qa_highlights.question: Will the labour issue be resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour is returning; normalisation expected by end-June. April-May utilisation affected, Q1 utilisation about 80%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 growth fall short of the 30% guided?
qa_highlights.answer: Khopoli exit cut 5,000-6,000 tonnes capacity; ~₹40 crore lower revenue from labour jobs; March LPG crisis delayed April-May completions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: On ₹115 crore net worth and ~₹38 crore steady-state fixed assets, management expects ROE of 17-19%.

risks_watch: Umargam expansion has slipped repeatedly (March to October); the transcript's '2025' completion references are inconsistent with the June 2026 call date.
Labour availability: migration after the March LPG crisis; normalisation hoped for end-June.
Single LPG supplier force majeure exposed supply risk; management now says multiple gas sources are available.
Steel and input-cost volatility; fixed conversion and transport costs not fully passed through.
Large rental and depreciation costs until new capacity is commissioned; finance cost ~₹15 crore vs. stated ~4% of turnover guidance.
Margin targets (12-13% normalised EBITDA; 7-8% PAT aspiration) well above reported 10.86% and ~3.5% PAT.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book and long-term aspiration, but candid on FY26 execution misses (LPG, labour, capex delay). Several guidance figures and dates were inconsistent within the call, and management deflected a question on realisation gap versus PEB by distinguishing business models.
key_quotes: We maintain a strong order book and feel confident about the way forward.
Our expansion will be finished by October this year.
Our PAT was 10.51 crores. This includes a one-time bad debt write-off of 1.65 crores and rental costs of 2.4 crores.

financial_highlights.change: Adds back bad debt, rent and Khopoli costs

financial_highlights.value: ~₹15 crore on ~₹80 crore borrowings (as referenced by analyst)
financial_highlights.change: Management expects ~4% of turnover in FY26
Production volume up 22% YoY including labour jobs

adds.what: 1 MW solar plant (power cost, not production capacity)
Khopoli facility exit removing ~5,000-6,000 tonnes capacity

growth.why: FY27 targets ₹400 crore revenue (about 33% over FY26's ~₹300 crore) and ₹500 crore+ order book, backed by order book rising from ~₹200 crore to ~₹350 crore and the Umargam expansion (30k to 54k tonnes), though the expansion slipped from March to October 2026 and the Khopoli exit removes ~5-6k tonnes.
